name: Bitfarms Ltd. (Keel Infrastructure)

profile.description: Bitfarms, redomiciled to the US and rebranded Keel Infrastructure around April 2026, is a bitcoin miner winding down mining over about two years to pivot to HPC and AI infrastructure. FY2025 revenue was $229M (+72%), but Q1 2026 revenue fell 23% YoY to $37.0M [1]. Yahoo data under BITF is unavailable, so metrics use the KEEL listing.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): announced a gradual wind-down of bitcoin mining to pivot to HPC and AI infrastructure, plus energy and heat-recycling diversification, a significant strategic pivot not yet proven in revenue [2]. AI Deployment (1/2): AI/HPC is under development, not yet shipping at scale. Market Share (0/2): a mid-tier miner without share leadership. Pipeline (1/2): US HPC/AI sites are being developed but no dated revenue visibility was found. R&D Intensity (0/1): no R&D disclosed.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): purpose is oriented around digital infrastructure and returns and has changed with the pivot [2]. Community Impact (0/2): no specific programs found; ESG appears as a risk-factor disclosure [3]. Employee Retention (0/2): little Glassdoor data (4 reviews) with mixed management feedback [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): no evidence of net insider buying.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Scored as a Growth stock using the KEEL listing. D/E of 316% (0), ROE of -75.6% (0, 2x), profit margin of -231% (0), revenue growth of -50% YoY (0) and negative forward P/E (0) all hit floors [1]. Only the roughly 35% 5-year revenue CAGR (1.0, 2x; $69M in 2021 to $229M in 2025) scores. PEG unavailable and excluded. Weighted score 2.0 of 8 equals 2.5, rounded up to 3. Daily dollar volume of about $121M passes the liquidity floor.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): HPC and AI data-center hosting is demand-side infrastructure that AI increases, and power-secured sites are scarce; a bitcoin miner is not threatened by AI. Management lists limited AI/HPC experience as a risk, and security from AI adoption is a concern [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): no meaningful AI revenue yet; revenue is still bitcoin mining.

infinite_game.summary: Bitfarms is executing a genuine strategic reinvention from bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure, which shows existential flexibility, but the pivot is driven by economics rather than a lasting cause, and the company has no articulated Just Cause beyond digital infrastructure growth.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): no articulated vision of a better future; the business exists to monetize power and compute and changed direction with market economics [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Great Place to Work certification (75% great place) and a collaborative family culture, offset by reactive management [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): no commentary found on learning from competitors.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): pivoting from bitcoin mining to HPC/AI infrastructure and rebranding as Keel Infrastructure redefines the company [1][2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): committing to wind down profitable-in-cycle mining over about two years to build HPC/AI is a costly long-term bet, though financing pressures were a driver [2].

investment_thesis: Bitfarms (now Keel Infrastructure) at $3.62 is a levered option on AI power infrastructure. FY2025 revenue rose 72% to $229M, power-secured North American sites are being redirected from bitcoin to HPC/AI, and management added US data-center experts to the leadership team [1][2]. If sites are leased at hyperscaler-grade contracts, the market could re-rate the company from miner to infrastructure owner.
thesis_continued: The bear case is execution and balance sheet: Q1 2026 revenue fell 23% YoY to $37.0M, TTM revenue growth is -50% per Yahoo, the profit margin is -231%, D/E is 316% and ROE is -75.6% [1]. Analysts trimmed revenue forecasts, and management lists limited HPC/AI experience as a risk factor [2]. Winding down mining removes cash flow before HPC revenue exists, so dilution or more debt is likely.
key_catalysts: Signing of HPC/AI tenant leases on converted power sites, providing contracted revenue visibility [2]
Redomiciliation and Keel Infrastructure rebrand attracting infrastructure-oriented investors [1]
Added US data-center leadership expertise to execute the HPC build [2]
key_risks: Revenue gap during the pivot: Q1 2026 revenue -23% YoY and mining wind-down before HPC revenue [1]
Leverage of 316% D/E and negative ROE of -75.6% raise financing and dilution risk [1]
Management's limited AI/HPC experience and competition from established data-center developers [2]
